title: A gate that measured nothing does not record a failure
description: A gate step that exits non-zero having collected nothing produced no verdict about the tests, and the ledger records it as a failing suite. Field report 12's operator read three such rows as contention, withdrew two of them on inspection, and the one that survived was a gate measuring while a sibling executor wrote files. The column that separates them - `ran` - was on the row the whole time. A signal-killed gate is classified correctly and then handed to the operator with no retry at any parallelism.
desiredOutcome: A recorded gate row says whether its steps measured anything, and a verdict of `failed` is reserved for a run that measured and found failures. A step that collected nothing is visible as such on the row; the gate verdict becomes `could-not-run` only when nothing was measured AND the tree carried dirty paths outside the declared scope at run start, with the basis naming them. A task whose own test file does not compile, with no foreign dirty paths, stays red - that case is proven red before either rule ships.

tasks.title: A step that collected nothing says so on the row
tasks.description: A step that exits non-zero having collected nothing is recorded as such on the evidence row - it is free, `ran` is already computed, and it is the fact a reader needs to tell a real failure from a run that never measured. This is the observation half only: the gate verdict does not change in this task. A field operator had three rows he read as contention, withdrew two on inspection, and the column that would have separated them at the time was already there.

add: plugins/audit/tests/test_run_test_gate.py: a non-zero step with ran 0 is recorded as having measured nothing; a step that measured and failed is not

tasks.title: could-not-run when nothing was measured and the tree was dirty outside scope
tasks.description: The gate verdict becomes `could-not-run` when nothing was measured AND the tree carried dirty paths outside the declared scope at run start - the condition under which a whole-program step's failure is not attributable to this task. `_porcelain` already lists every dirty path before the run and `dirty_digest` already counts them; the mutation bracket's owned/foreign split is the reasoning to reuse. The case that must STAY RED is a task whose own test file does not compile with no foreign dirty paths, and it is proven red before the rule ships - that is F323's class, real failures excused as infrastructure.

add: plugins/audit/tests/test_run_test_gate.py: nothing measured plus foreign dirty paths is could-not-run; nothing measured with a clean foreign tree stays failed

tasks.title: A red gate names what failed
tasks.description: A red gate records that the suite failed and how many checks ran, never WHICH tests failed. Three field reports name the same cost; two operators wrote their own failing-test reporter around the gate rather than read the record. The runner's own output is read for the path scan and for the check count and then dropped - it reaches neither the result nor the row. Twice an operator had a red gate and no way to act on it from the record, recovering the names from a project artefact the next run overwrites. Parse the failing names where the summary reader recognises the runner, else keep a capped tail, and put them on the row as an observation.

add: plugins/audit/tests/test_run_test_gate.py: a jest-shaped red gate records the failing suite and test names; an unrecognised runner records a capped tail rather than silence
